# Contract: the token surface
<!-- Generated by /speckit.plan Phase 1 -->

The custom-property names components may rely on. This is the API of `@fablab/ui`: adding a
token is additive, **renaming or removing one is a breaking change** for every consumer.

## The rule that matters most

**Exactly one colour token is per-organization.**

| Token | Value | Who sets it |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-primary` | `theme.primaryColor`, defaulting to `--color-rosa-raw` | **Per organization** (CLR-001) |
| `--color-navy` `--color-azul` `--color-teal` `--color-amarelo` `--color-laranja` `--color-claro` | fixed hexes | Platform — identical for every organization |
| `--color-rosa-raw` | `#EE9DC4` | **Private.** The default for `--color-primary`. Components may not use it and lint rejects them if they try |

> **There is no `--color-rosa` for components to reach for.** The raw pink is
> `--color-rosa-raw`, it is private, and lint rejects its use outside `tokens/`.
>
> *(Revised after review round 1.)* The first draft exported `--color-rosa` and relied on a
> documented convention. That was unenforceable and the failure mode is invisible: a CTA
> using it renders **identically** for CITe, passes every test, and fails to co-brand only
> once a second organization exists. It was the plan's own top risk with nothing behind it.
> Renaming the token makes reaching for it visibly wrong, and the lint rule makes it fail.

## Colour

```css
--color-navy    /* #191C37  base background, text on light */
--color-azul    /* #3760AA  links, icons, graphic elements  */
--color-teal    /* #74B7A5  hero band, progress detail, status chips */
--color-amarelo /* #F8C810  XP, rewards, mission icons, numbering */
--color-laranja /* #EE703E  the canonical logo chip */
--color-rosa-raw /* #EE9DC4  PRIVATE — the default for --color-primary; not for components */
--color-claro   /* #DCE7E3  light surfaces, text on dark */
--color-primary /* per-organization accent: CTAs, active tabs, card titles */
```

Backgrounds are named by role rather than colour, so the white-background pages
(`docs/product/visual-identity.md` § Paleta) do not need per-page overrides:

```css
--surface-page      /* navy by default */
--surface-card
--surface-inverted  /* the white content area used by Biblioteca 3D and Aulas */
--text-on-dark  --text-on-light
```

## Typography

```css
--font-display  /* Aldo the Apache → condensed sans fallback. Logo, logotype, headings */
--font-body     /* Comfortaa      → system-ui, sans-serif                              */
--text-xs … --text-3xl
```

**There are two faces and two tokens.** Both ship in the repository, so CI renders the same
typography production does.

> **`--font-logotype` was removed** *(designer decision, 2026-08-27)*. It named SquareFont
> for the "CITE BAURU" logotype; Aldo the Apache now covers that role, so the token would
> have held the same value as `--font-display`.
>
> Keeping both would repeat the `--color-rosa` mistake one section above: two names for one
> value, where picking the wrong one renders **identically** and no test can tell. And unlike
> the colour case there is no future divergence to reserve a seam for — CLR-001 already fixed
> that exactly one token varies per organization, and it is `--color-primary`.
>
> This is a breaking change to the contract, made when the contract has **zero consumers**
> (`packages/ui` still exports `{}`). It is free today and expensive after the components exist.

Both faces declare `font-display: swap` and a real fallback stack — now for latency (feature
003's LCP budget) rather than for a missing file, since no file is missing.

## Layout

```css
--bp-mobile   /* 390  */
--bp-tablet   /* 834  */
--bp-desktop  /* 1440 */
--space-1 … --space-12   --radius-sm --radius-md   --shadow-hard
```

Breakpoints are tokens so a media query never contains a bare number — the three values are
*design targets* from the mockups, not arbitrary thresholds, and naming them keeps that
traceable.

## Documented contrast pairs

`tokens/index.ts` exports `DOCUMENTED_PAIRS`, and `contrast.test.ts` iterates it (SC-006).
**A pair that fails WCAG AA cannot be documented** — which is the mechanism that finally
answers the open question in `visual-identity.md` § Paleta about pink-on-navy small text.

## What `@fablab/ui` may never import

Inherited from feature 000 and extended (FR-018): no `payload`, no `@payloadcms/*`, no Next
*server* APIs, no IO. The package receives resolved values as props or custom properties.
Its React dependency is a **peer** — the app owns the React instance.
